headline: Computational omics frameworks for biomarker discovery and microbial network inference
label: Multi Omics Computational Modeling
summary: Multi-omics and machine learning approaches are being benchmarked and applied to identify candidate biomarkers in sepsis, MASLD, and microbial communities.
synthesis: The shared thread is computational inference from high-dimensional omics measurements, with methods evaluated against simulated or cohort data before biological interpretation. A preprint benchmarks network-impact and dissimilarity-overlap methods against alpha/beta-diversity and neural network baselines using GLV-simulated single-time-point microbial samples. A published study pairs widely targeted metabolomics with machine learning to identify succinate as a key metabolite in sepsis-associated encephalopathy. Another examines plasma and liver tissue proteomics to assess plasma biomarkers for MASH within MASLD. A statistical comparison of univariate and multivariate multi-omics dimension-reduction methods for outcome modelling is evaluated via simulations and BMI data. What is new here is the explicit, head-to-head evaluation of integration and inference choices, rather than descriptive omics output alone.
